prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the camera wearer’s forearms and hands are consistently the nearest surfaces, about 0.2–0.6 m away, while the rope and carabiner are at a similar reach distance near the upper centre/right. The rock face and ground lie roughly 0.5–2 m in front and below, with a second person only partly visible near the top edge at approximately 1–2 m; equipment on the left is roughly 1–2 m away. The arms rise and shift from centre-right toward the centre across the sequence, increasingly occluding the rope, rock, and equipment, while the other person remains cropped and mostly behind the foreground arms. The depth map makes near-versus-far layering clearer than RGB, but its nearly black distant regions, blurred object boundaries, and inconsistent brightness on the rock and small ropes make metric distances and motion uncertain.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map primarily isolates the camera wearer’s two foreground arms/hands as large person masks, showing that they occupy the centre and right foreground and overlap each other near the raised hands. It also marks a backpack or equipment bundle left of centre in an early frame and several partial person regions at the far left, top edge, and far right, corresponding to people or body parts that are cropped or heavily occluded. Across the frames, the two arm masks move upward and inward, then toward the right, while the backpack disappears from view and additional narrow person masks enter at the right edge; relative distances are not encoded, although RGB and mask size suggest the arms are within about 0.2–0.6 m and the other person/equipment about 1–2 m away. The map clarifies which visible regions belong to separate instances despite overlap, but it is unreliable around hands, ropes, gaps between the arms, and frame boundaries, with fragmented masks, duplicate person labels, missed equipment, and some likely misclassified regions; facing direction and gaze are not recoverable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only sparse magenta hand skeletons: one near the upper centre in the second frame, paired hand structures near the upper-right/centre in the fourth frame, and a partial hand near the upper-right in the fifth frame. These detections place the camera wearer’s raised hands close together around the rope/carabiner area, roughly 0.3–0.6 m from the camera, and show them shifting rightward across the sequence; no usable yellow body skeleton is visible. The hand keypoints reveal finger and wrist configuration more clearly than RGB where skin, rope, and hardware overlap, but the first and third frames have no detection and the final detection is incomplete. Because the other person’s body and face are not detected, this map cannot reliably establish that person’s orientation, gaze, reach, inter-person distance, or whether anyone is in front of or behind another beyond the foreground placement of the detected hands.
